prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1319; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a low-speed head-on collision. The insured's vehicle and the other vehicle were both reported as having front-end damage, and the claimant, who is represented by counsel, has been identified as the injured occupant.

Entry 2: Police report and two independent witness statements confirm the collision occurred as described and that the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the time. Scene photographs were reviewed and are consistent with the reported impact.

Entry 3: Vehicle damage was inspected and the pattern matches the described frontal impact. No prior damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing in file records suggests the damage predates the policy coverage start.

Entry 4: The driver is named on the policy and coverage is confirmed for the date of loss. The claimant's account of events has remained the same across every contact to date, including the initial call and the recorded interview.

Entry 5: Medical records reflect a wrist fracture, which is a plausible injury for this type of collision. Records also show a small strain to the same area several years ago that healed fully and was not treated as an ongoing condition.

Entry 6: Treatment followed a typical course, with orthopedic follow-up and physical therapy, and tapered off as the claimant's range of motion and strength improved. Billing has been reviewed against the treatment notes and appears in line with the care provided.

Entry 7: Based on the current file, the injury and treatment appear consistent with the loss. Counsel has been advised of the review status, and the file will remain open pending receipt of the final medical bills.
